verdict: OK to lend in Sanand auto components — pursue Tier-2 EV/powertrain-agnostic suppliers with tight covenants; avoid single-OEM, ICE-engine-dependent job-workers.
title: Sanand auto & auto components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Sanand is an OEM-anchored cluster: vehicle and engine plants pulling a ring of component and sub-assembly suppliers around them [3]. A component maker buys steel, aluminium and bought-out parts, converts them on presses and machining lines, and sells on schedule to one or two OEMs. **Cash is made on the conversion margin, not on the metal — so the spread between input cost and the price the OEM agrees to pay is the whole business.** Pricing power sits with the OEM; the supplier absorbs commodity swings unless the contract has a pass-through clause. ICRA's methodology flags exactly this: hedging policy and commodity exposure relative to profits is a core credit test [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the pass-through clause and the hedging policy; if aluminium or steel is a large share of raw material and there is no pass-through, ask for the last three quarters' gross margin to see who ate the squeeze.

## Where cash sits and what has changed
Working capital is the trap. Gross current assets have averaged 160-170 days in recent years for component makers [10], and rating guidance treats debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times as a stretch [10]. **A supplier can be profitable and still short of cash because receivables from a large OEM run long while payables to steel mills run short.** On the ground, Sanand's story is EV capacity: Tata Motors' takeover of the Ford Sanand plant carried a stated plan to make 2 lakh EVs annually by 2026 with additional investment of Rs 2,000 crore [3] — note this source is old and the 2026 milestone should be verified with the customer, not assumed. Locally, hiring for auto-component sales support in Sanand continues [2], a small but real sign the supplier base is still staffing up.

## The growth opportunity to pursue now
Nationally, IIP for NIC 29 output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and Gujarat GST collections are running +11.9% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D]. **Pursue the powertrain-agnostic supplier — braking, aluminium lightweighting, interiors — because that is where peer order books are actually filling.** ASK Automotive's Q1 FY27 order wins include EV components across braking and aluminium lightweighting [5]; Motherson Sumi Wiring grew revenue 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore and net profit 35% to Rs 223 crore in Q2 [4]; Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its growth target [7]. Avoid the pure ICE engine-part job-worker: CRISIL warns engine-focused suppliers face higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11].
Cap debt/EBITDA at 2.5 times in covenant [10]. Take quarterly commodity-cost reconciliation against the pass-through clause. For capex, insist on an order-backed tranche, not a lump sum.

## Early-warning signs
- **Receivable days stretching past the 160-170 day norm [10] (monthly)** -> freeze fresh limits and ask for the OEM payment correspondence. - **Gross margin falling while aluminium or steel rises (quarterly)** -> check pass-through clause enforcement; if absent, reprice or exit. - **Debt/EBITDA crossing 2.5 times [10] (quarterly)** -> move to secured, amortising structure. - **Sanand EV ramp slipping past the stated 2026 milestone [3] (quarterly)** -> re-base the borrower's volume assumptions with them.
